episodes.197316: A storm system passing to the north of southern New England brought several inches of rain along with strong winds which caused a smattering of damage in MA and RI.
episodes.197471: Thunderstorms embedded within a squall line ahead of an approaching cold front produce gusty winds across Tampa Bay waters.
episodes.197474: A strong cold front produced a strongly-forced line of thunderstorms. This line of thunderstorms produced mainly sub-severe wind gusts, with one exception near the Bowie area for a brief time in the mid afternoon.
episodes.197564: A strong cold front shifting across the region within a high shear/low CAPE environment produced showers capable of damaging wind gusts across coastal waters.
episodes.197722: A strong cold front moved through the region in the afternoon and evening. Ahead of the front, widespread showers moved across central North Carolina. While the majority of the showers were non-severe, a few isolated damaging wind reports were observed in Nash and Johnston Counties.
episodes.198507: A cold front crossed the region during the mid-morning hours of December 11, 2024. Behind this front, winds increased significantly from the west-northwest. Some of these winds were strong enough to cause damage in the form of downed trees and power lines. Portions on Henry, Carroll, and Pittsylvania Counties reported trees down. Two power lines came down in Carroll County.  Heavy rain occurred during the early morning hours of the day across Patrick County, with anywhere between 2.75 inches and 3.50 inches falling across the foothills of the Blue Ridge.  Rainfall rates were observed at around 1 inch of rain per hour with the passage of the heavy rain.  This resulted in minor stream flooding across portions of Patrick County.

events.narrative: The Patrick County Schools Superintendent reported that Maple Swamp Road was flooded by Maple Swamp Creek, and partially impassible.  No damage was reported to the road, which was reopened to traffic after the flooding receded.

The Patrick County Schools Superintendent reported that a portion of Quebec Spring Road was flooded and impassible.  No damage to the road was reported, and the road was reopened to traffic after the flooding receded.
